fields.name: control

fields.name: war
doc: // Optional sibling to `payload`, `media`, and `control`. Carries the

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayControlSealKeyEnvelope
doc: /// Computer Use control-plane payload — see Phase 8/9/12 of
/// `plans/2026-05-16-computer-use-master-plan.md`. Fields are mutually
/// optional so a single struct can carry any of the four control frame
/// types without forcing receivers to learn about cases they don't yet
/// support. The `kind` discriminator pairs with the outer frame's
/// `HermesRealtimeRelayFrameType` for explicit dispatch.
/// F10 — the sealKeyV3-wrapped control-frame-seal session key, carried once on
/// `control.classify` when both peers advertise `control_seal_v1`. The Mac
/// opens it with its relay private key + the phone's PINNED relay sender key
/// (same pinning as the chat lane) and both sides derive the AES-GCM seal key
/// via `ControlFrameSeal.deriveSessionKey`. Pre-F10 receivers ignore the field.

fields.name: senderPeerNodeId
doc: /// The peerNodeId the phone PUBLISHED in `relay_sender_keys/{deviceId}` —
/// the Mac's trust resolver matches it during pinned-key lookup. This is
/// the relay sender identity, NOT the phone-control controller peerNodeId
/// (which is bound separately into the wrap AAD).

fields.name: controlSealKey
doc: /// F10 — sealKeyV3-wrapped seal-session key, sent once on `control.classify`.

fields.name: sealedFrameBase64
doc: /// F10 — when present, this payload's real content rides inside: a
/// `ControlFrameSeal` envelope (OBCFS1) over the JSON of the inner
/// `HermesRealtimeRelayControlPayload`, AAD-bound to (peerNodeId,
/// frame type). `streamClass` stays visible for routing; everything else
/// is confidential. Pre-F10 receivers see an empty payload and ignore it.

types.name: PhoneControlSigningKeyKind
doc: /// Which signing-key custody class produced an authority envelope's signature
/// (F2 hardware-bind). `ed25519` (or an absent `keyKind` on the wire, for
/// backward compatibility with pre-F2 controllers) is the legacy software
/// CryptoKit Curve25519 key. `secureEnclaveP256` is a non-exportable NIST
/// P-256 key held in the iOS Secure Enclave / Android StrongBox Keystore; its
/// `signatureEd25519` field carries a raw (r‖s) 64-byte ECDSA-over-SHA256
/// signature instead of an Ed25519 signature. The field name is historical —
/// it is the signature carrier regardless of algorithm, mirroring the
/// `intentHashBlake3`/`attestationHashBlake3` naming.

fields.name: attestationHashBlake3
doc: /// Optional App Attest / Play Integrity digest bound into capability-token minting (WS2).

fields.name: keyKind
doc: /// F2: which key-custody class signed this envelope. Absent ⇒ `.ed25519`
/// (legacy software key). Present `se-p256` ⇒ the signature is a raw
/// P-256 ECDSA signature from a Secure Enclave / StrongBox key.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelaySessionGrantChallenge
doc: /// Versioned Linux-host challenge asking a paired phone to issue an
/// existing agent grant bound to one exact Computer Use session intent.
/// The phone must validate every field before authenticating or signing.

fields.name: beforeScreenshotPNGBase64
doc: /// Optional PNG evidence captured immediately before the requested
/// action. This lets daemon-originated browser approvals render the
/// same pre-action thumbnail as app-owned Mac approvals without a
/// second file-transfer round trip.

fields.name: trustMode
doc: /// Optional `ComputerUseTrustMode.rawValue` for approval surfaces
/// that need to reveal Step-only affordances such as burst approval.
/// Older clients can omit this field and render Manual behavior.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelaySystemPermissionKind
doc: /// macOS Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) buckets the System
/// Permission Concierge knows how to grant remotely. Carried over the
/// existing Computer Use control stream; older peers ignore the new
/// frame types because the outer envelope is forward-compatible.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelaySystemPermissionStatusKind
doc: /// Live status of a single TCC bucket as observed by the Mac. The Mac
/// emits one frame per (kind, bundleId) change and one optimistic frame
/// when it starts servicing a request.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelaySystemPermissionAction
doc: /// Mac-side action the phone wants run for a permission kind. The Mac
/// receiver gates the action against the bundled `kind`.
/// Trigger the macOS native prompt (CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess,
/// AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions(prompt: true), AVCaptureDevice
/// requestAccess) when one exists. No-op for FDA.
/// Open the matching System Settings deep link via NSWorkspace.
/// Native prompt + deep link in one shot. Default behaviour for kinds
/// that benefit from both (Screen Recording is the canonical case —
/// the prompt seeds the TCC entry, the deep link finishes the job).
/// Run a polling probe-read only; no UI side effects. Used by the
/// monitor at startup to populate the latest status without touching
/// System Settings.
/// Once the related TCC bucket flips to granted, re-dispatch the
/// original failed tool call. The Mac honors this only when the
/// originating tool call is still inflight.

fields.name: bundleId
doc: /// Required for `kind == .automation` (target bundle id, e.g.
/// `com.apple.Notes`). Optional for all other kinds.

fields.name: originatingToolCallId
doc: /// Tool call id this request is trying to unblock. Carried verbatim
/// in the resulting status frames so the iOS retry dispatcher and
/// the Mac retry hook can pair the request with the original
/// inflight tool invocation.

fields.name: deepLink
doc: /// System Settings deep link — `x-apple.systempreferences:` URL the
/// phone displays as a fallback and that the Mac can re-open on its
/// own when handling a request.

fields.name: instructions
doc: /// Human-readable steps to render in the iOS sheet ("Open System
/// Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording → toggle
/// OpenBurnBar"). Optional — iOS has shipped defaults per kind.

fields.name: failureCategory
doc: /// Compact category tag for the classifier or the failing tool
/// (e.g. `"tccd"`, `"AXIsProcessTrusted"`, `"AppleEvents"`). Used by
/// telemetry and the Mac audit chain — not surfaced in the iOS sheet.

fields.name: targetKind
doc: /// Smart Zoom target type. Optional so older peers without
/// Smart Zoom continue to decode the existing focus payload.

fields.name: displayId
doc: /// Display the rect/point belong to. Matches
/// `HermesRealtimeRelayDisplayDescriptor.id` so the phone can ignore
/// context that targets a display it is not currently mirroring.

fields.name: normalizedRect
doc: /// Target rectangle expressed in display-relative normalized
/// coordinates `[0...1]`. Used for text-field, window, and agent
/// workspace targets.

fields.name: normalizedPoint
doc: /// Target point expressed in display-relative normalized
/// coordinates `[0...1]`. Used for cursor targets where a rect
/// would be Mac-side guesswork.

fields.name: confidence
doc: /// Provider's confidence in the target. `1.0` for direct AX hits,
/// lower values for fallbacks like window-from-cursor.

fields.name: updatedAt
doc: /// Wall-clock timestamp the provider sampled the target. Used by

fields.name: streamClass
doc: /// Identifier of the media stream class this frame addresses

fields.name: attachment

fields.name: blobTicket

fields.name: ack

fields.name: focusContext

fields.name: sealedFramePosition

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelaySealedMediaFramePosition
doc: /// F7 — the cleartext AAD components of a sealed media frame (the frame's

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayAgentTerminalRequest
doc: /// Mercury Phase 8 — iOS-initiated request asking the Mac to start
/// hosting a screen share (or, in future phases, another mirrorable
/// stream class). The Mac arbitrates via `MercuryRouter` and replies
/// with `HermesRealtimeRelayMirrorAck`. Decision 2 in
/// `project_media_rollout`: the Mac is the only gate. No authority
/// envelope is required — the iroh pairing already authenticates the
/// requester.
/// Optional Phase 12 request to launch an agent's CLI **interactively** in a
/// visible Mac Terminal and pin the mirror to that single Terminal window,
/// rather than mirroring the full display. When present (and `interactive`),
/// the Mac launches `runtimeId`'s CLI, resolves the new Terminal window's
/// `CGWindowID`, and starts a window-pinned capture. Older Mac peers that do
/// not know this field keep their existing full-display mirror behavior.

fields.name: runtimeId
doc: /// CLI runtime identifier (e.g. `codex`, `claude`, `droid`, `forge`,
/// `antigravity`, `grok`, `hermes`, `pi`). Carried as a string for
/// forward-compat with runtimes the Mac may not yet recognize.

fields.name: workingDirectory
doc: /// Optional working directory to `cd` into before launching the CLI.

fields.name: interactive
doc: /// Whether to launch an interactive REPL/TUI (true) vs a one-shot run.
/// Only `true` drives the window-pinned focused-terminal flow.

fields.name: modelID
doc: /// Optional model identifier to pass to the CLI.

fields.name: requestId
doc: /// iOS-generated UUID. Echoed in the ack for correlation.

fields.name: requestedAt
doc: /// Clock skew is tolerated by the Mac — informational only.

fields.name: requesterDisplayName
doc: /// Display name shown on the Mac's `IncomingCallSheet` ("Alberto's iPhone").

fields.name: streamClass
doc: /// Which `MediaStreamClass` the requester wants opened (default
/// `media.screen.video`). Carried as a string for forward-compat
/// with future mirrorable surfaces.

fields.name: streamingCapabilities
doc: /// Optional Phase 0/2 streaming probe snapshot from the requester.
/// Older peers omit this field; the Mac falls back to the last
/// heartbeat or the existing v1 behavior when it is absent.

fields.name: focusFollowMode
doc: /// Optional Phase 5 focus-follow preference from the phone. Mac peers
/// that do not know it keep their existing full-display mirror behavior.

fields.name: remoteUnlockSession
doc: /// Optional Remote Unlock request metadata. Presence is not enough to
/// start unlock; the embedded authority must still validate on the Mac.

fields.name: agentTerminal
doc: /// Optional Phase 12 interactive-CLI request. When present (and
/// `interactive`), the Mac launches the runtime's CLI in a visible
/// Terminal and pins the mirror to that single window. Older peers omit
/// this field and keep the existing full-display mirror behavior.

fields.name: mediaSealKey
doc: /// F7 — sealKeyV3-wrapped media-frame-AEAD session key, present when the
/// requester wants per-frame sealing and both peers advertise
/// `media_frame_aead_v1`. Pre-F7 Macs ignore it (frames stay plaintext at
/// the app layer over the iroh transport seal).

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayMirrorAck
doc: /// Mercury Phase 8 — Mac-side reply to a `HermesRealtimeRelayMirrorRequest`.

fields.name: detail
doc: /// Free-text reason surfaced in the iOS Mercury Live sheet banner.

fields.name: cooldownSecondsRemaining
doc: /// Populated only when `decision == .coolingDown`. Omitted from the
/// wire form otherwise to preserve byte-identical encoding when the
/// field is absent (see `MirrorAckEncodingTests`).

fields.name: streamingCapabilities
doc: /// F7: the host's streaming capability snapshot (codecs, wire versions,
/// frame-AEAD support) so the viewer can negotiate without an extra round
/// trip. Optional — pre-F7 hosts omit it and pre-F7 viewers ignore it.

fields.name: mediaFrameSealEstablished
doc: /// True only when the Mac accepted this mirror request and opened the
/// request's media-frame seal key, so screen frames for this session will
/// be sealed. Absent means legacy plaintext remains possible.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayMirrorStop
doc: /// Mercury Phase 8 — requester-side end signal for an accepted mirror session.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayCallInvite
doc: /// Mercury phone-originated call invite. This is the cross-platform
/// sibling of the Mac -> phone PushKit/FCM call path: it rides the live
/// `media.control` stream so an already-awake Mac can surface a real
/// incoming-call prompt without needing a cloud wake.

fields.name: callKind
doc: /// `"video"` today; kept as a string so future audio-only/group-call
/// invites do not break older clients.

fields.name: mediaSealKey
doc: /// F7 — sealKeyV3-wrapped media-frame-AEAD session key for the
/// accepted call. A call must not start native capture unless

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayCallAck
doc: /// Mac-side response to `HermesRealtimeRelayCallInvite`.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayPresenceHeartbeat
doc: /// Mercury Phase 8 — periodic iOS → Mac beacon so the Mac knows it has
/// a live mirrorable client (used for outbound triggers like "Call
/// iPhone" from the Mac popover). Sent every 60s once the iOS control
/// stream is `live`. Forward-compatible: unknown capability strings are
/// dropped silently by `MercuryPeer.Feature` decoding.

fields.name: errorCode
doc: /// Public, non-sensitive terminal error code for `response.error` frames.
/// Do not put user/provider/runtime text here; encrypted `.error` chunks carry
/// private detail when the caller needs it.

fields.name: error
doc: /// Legacy plaintext error text kept decodable for older peers. New iroh
/// senders must not populate this on `response.error` frames.

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayWarDenialReason

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayWarRunStatus
doc: /// Terminal and intermediate states for a dispatched run, as reported back

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayWarBodyState

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayWarDispatchRequest
doc: /// A unit of work routed to a peer Mac. Carries the originator so the
/// receiving machine can stamp the run it starts, which is what the Command

types.name: HermesRealtimeRelayWarPayload
doc: /// War Room Wire payload — the Mac⇄Mac fleet lane.
/// Fields are mutually optional so one struct carries any of the eight war
/// frames without forcing a receiver to learn cases it does not support,
/// matching the Computer Use control payload's shape. The `kind`
/// discriminator pairs with the outer frame's `HermesRealtimeRelayFrameType`
/// for explicit dispatch.

fields.name: pairId
doc: /// The canonical `war_wire_grants` document id the dialer is claiming.
/// The answering Mac re-derives it and refuses a mismatch rather than
/// trusting the dialer's arithmetic.

fields.name: sequence
doc: /// Monotonic per-run chunk ordinal. The receiver drops a chunk that
/// arrives out of order rather than splicing output incorrectly.
